Defining mandibulofacial dysostosis, macroblepharon/ectropion and macrostomia involve skeleton, eyelids and mouth; ear involvement lacks frequency evidence.
Developmental impairment and structural ocular abnormalities are principal features; other organ malformations are variably reported without frequency support.
Premature activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal endocrine axis; accelerated skeletal maturation alone does not establish skeletal damage.
Acquired progressive lymphangioma is a dermal lymphatic vascular proliferation producing persistent skin plaques.
Developmental delay and central tone abnormalities occur in 8/8; esotropia is 2/8 and individual contractures 1/8, below threshold.
Histoplasma-associated inflammation of the pericardium defines cardiac and infectious involvement.
Lymphoid-cell malignancy warrants haematologic and lymphoma mechanism axes; testicular origin has no reproductive axis.
The syndrome is defined by neurologic disease, endocrine dysfunction and exocrine pancreatic disease.
Capsule-confined thymic epithelial tumour; thymus has no listed anatomical axis. Thymoma itself is neither lymphoma nor an autoimmune disease.
Benign tumour arising in an extrahepatic bile duct, explicitly covered by the hepatic axis.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and brain abnormalities are frequent; palate and pinna shape abnormalities alone do not establish functional damage.
Primary skeletal muscular dystrophy; cerebral white-matter abnormalities occur in 6/6 and seizures in 4/5, supporting substantial neurologic involvement.
Structural obstruction of the lacrimal drainage apparatus.
Bile-acid synthesis disorder with hepatic injury; developmental impairment and ataxia in 1/1 reported patient support neurologic involvement, with limited sampling.
Explicitly HPV-driven carcinoma supports the infectious mechanism axis; penile reproductive origin has no anatomical axis here.
C1q-associated autoimmune lupus commonly affects skin (~90%) and kidneys (~30-40%); arthritis is less consistent than in ordinary SLE.
Congenital cardiac malformations, particularly VSD, are principal organ defects; other anomalies vary and lack evidence of common functional involvement.
Benign infiltrative fibro-fatty tumour arising in subcutis and connective soft tissues of the extremities, especially hands and feet.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability are common across this variable duplication group; no other common organ damage is established.
Inherited coagulation-protein disorder causing bleeding; coagulation is explicitly haematologic.
Profound developmental encephalopathy with central hypotonia; persistent esotropia occurs in 3/4. Contractures and scoliosis are occasional.
Severe osteochondrodysplasia with short bones, vertebral and pelvic abnormalities; thoracic skeletal hypoplasia alone does not establish pulmonary damage.
Pathological distention of the stomach defines the disease; underlying causes do not establish additional organ involvement.
Defective thyroid-hormone deiodination produces a metabolic endocrine biochemical disorder despite clinical euthyroidism.
